# Summary and questions



# Z2 LGT Hamiltonian and its variants

A $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge field typically use Hamiltonian and Gauss's law;
$$
\begin{align*}
H &= -h \sum_{j} (\tau^z_{\ell} a^\dagger_j a_{j+1}  + \text{h.c.}) - K \sum_{\ell} \tau^x_{\ell} -\mu (-1)^{j}{a_j^\dagger a_j},\\
G_x &= (-1)^{a_j^\dagger a_j} \prod_{\ell \ni x} \tau^x_{\ell} 
\end{align*}
$$
Except for $Z_2$ LGT, the truncated version U(1) LGT is closely related to the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ LGT. To be specific, 

$$
\begin{align*}
H_{U(1)} &= − w  \sum_{j=1}^{L-1} (\Phi^\dagger_j U_{j,j+1}\Phi_{j+1} + h.c.) + m\sum_{j=1}^{L} (−1)^j\Phi^\dagger_j \Phi_j  +J \sum_{j=1}^{L-1} E^2_{j,j+1},\\
G_x &= E_{j,j+1} - E_{j-1,j} - \Phi^\dagger_j \Phi_{j} -  \frac{1 - (-1)^j}{2},
\end{align*}
$$
where $\Phi_j$ is fermionic operator support on site $j$ and $E_{j,j+1} = \sigma^z_{j,j+1}$ and $U_{j,j+1} = \sigma^{+}_{j,j+1}$ is the electric field and gauge field support on edge $(j,j+1)$.
These two Hamiltonians can be related by the Jordan-Wigner transformation:
$$
\begin{align*}
a_n = \left[\prod_{m < n} (-1)^{\Phi_m^\dagger \Phi_m}\right] \Phi_n.
\end{align*}
$$

# Optical lattice encoding

The first encoding method @schweizer2019floquet uses the state $\ket{f} := \ket{F = 1, m_F = +1} , \, \ket{a} := \ket{F = 1, m_F = -1}$ and corresponding annihilation operators $f_i^\dagger, a_i^\dagger$ support on each site $i$.
$$
f_j :=\ket{0}_j\bra{f}_j, \quad a_j :=\ket{0}_j\bra{a}_j
$$
To transform $f_j$ into a link operator rather than supports on sites,
restriciton $f_j ^\dagger f_j + f_{j+1}^\dagger f_{j+1} = 1, \forall j$ is needed,
and further transformed into valid Pauli matrices.
In the case of two-site system, this condition is always satisfied.
In this case, the link operator is given by the link $\langle 1,2 \rangle$:
$$
\tau^z_{\langle 1,2 \rangle } = f_2^\dagger f_2 - f_1^\dagger f_1, \quad \tau^x_{\langle 1,2 \rangle } = f_1^\dagger f_2 + f_2^\dagger f_1
$$


In the optical lattice, the physical Hamiltonian is restricted to the form
$$
\begin{align*}
H_{\mathrm{phy}} (t) = H_0(t) + V,
H_0(t) &= U \sum_{j=1,2} n_j^a n_j^f + \Delta_f n_1^f + A \cos(\omega t + \phi) (n_1^a + n_1^f),\\
V &= -J(a_2^\dagger a_1 + f_2^\dagger f_1 + \text{H.c.}),\\
N_a\;&\equiv\;n_1^a+n_2^a\;=\;1,\qquad N_f\;\equiv\;n_1^f+n_2^f\;=\;1,
\end{align*}
$$
where $\Delta_f$ comes from a magnetic field splitting the $f$ and $a$ states and $A \cos(\omega t + \phi)$ is the  oscillation of the laser frequency.
Floquet engineering is then used to generate an $H_{\mathrm{eff}}$ from $H_{\mathrm{phy}} (t)$.

:::{#lem-floquet_double_well .callout-important icon="false"}
## Floquet-renormalized tunneling in the two-species double well

The effective Hamiltonian expands as
$$
H_{\mathrm{eff}}^{(0)}\;=\;H_a^{(0)}+H_f^{(0)},
$$
both hoppings dressed by occupation-selective Bessel coefficients in the dimensionless drive amplitude $\chi\equiv A/(\hbar\omega)$. The matter $a$-hopping is selected by the one-photon channels $\nu=\pm 1$ on the two $f$-position projectors $P^f_\pm:\,n_1^f-n_2^f=\pm 1$,
$$
H_a^{(0)} \;=\; -J\Bigl[\,\mathcal J_{+1}(\chi)\,e^{+i\phi}\,P^f_+ \;+\; \mathcal J_{-1}(\chi)\,e^{-i\phi}\,P^f_-\,\Bigr]\,a_2^\dagger a_1 \;+\; \mathrm{H.c.}
$$
When additionally $\Delta_f=U$, the link-qubit $f$-hopping is selected by the zero- and two-photon channels $\nu=0,\,2$ on the two $a$-position projectors $P^a_0,P^a_2$ (sectors with $f$-hop energy mismatch $0$ and $2U$, respectively),
$$
H_f^{(0)} \;=\; -J\Bigl[\,\mathcal J_0(\chi)\,P^a_0 \;+\; \mathcal J_2(\chi)\,e^{2i\phi}\,P^a_2\,\Bigr]\,f_2^\dagger f_1 \;+\; \mathrm{H.c.}
$$
No fine-tuning of $\phi$ or $\chi$ is assumed at this stage; the further conditions $\phi=0$ and $\mathcal J_0(\chi)=\mathcal J_2(\chi)$ that collapse this operator-valued hopping to the gauge-invariant $\mathbb Z_2$ LGT belong to the matching discussion below.
:::


:::{.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Proof sketch

**Step 1 — Split into diagonal and hopping pieces.** Write $H_{\mathrm{phy}}(t)=H_0(t)+V$ with $H_0(t)$ the diagonal (number-operator) piece and $V=-J(a_2^\dagger a_1+f_2^\dagger f_1+\mathrm{H.c.})$ the off-diagonal hopping. Since $H_0(t)$ is diagonal in the Fock basis, every term commutes with every other and the rotating-frame generator below does not require time ordering — $H_0(t)$ assigns each Fock configuration a time-dependent c-number phase.

**Step 2 — Rotating frame.** Pass to $\ket{\tilde\psi(t)}=W(t)\ket\psi(t)$ with
$$
W(t)\;=\;\exp\!\left[\,\frac{i}{\hbar}\!\int_0^t\!H_0(t')\,dt'\,\right]\;=\;\exp\!\left[\,\frac{i}{\hbar}\!\left(U\!\!\sum_{j=1,2}\!n_j^a n_j^f\,t \,+\, \Delta_f n_1^f\,t \,+\, \tfrac{A}{\omega}\sin(\omega t+\phi)(n_1^a+n_1^f)\right)\!\right].
$$
The rotating-frame Hamiltonian is
$$
\widetilde H(t)\;=\;i\hbar\,\dot W(t)\,W^\dagger(t)\;+\;W(t)\,H_{\mathrm{phy}}(t)\,W^\dagger(t)\;=\;W(t)\,V\,W^\dagger(t),
$$
since the $i\hbar\dot W W^\dagger$ piece cancels the diagonal $W H_0(t) W^\dagger=H_0(t)$ exactly.

**Step 3 — Operator-valued dynamical phases.** Using the on-site identity $e^{i\lambda n}\,a\,e^{-i\lambda n}=e^{-i\lambda}a$,
$$
W(t)\,a_2^\dagger a_1\,W^\dagger(t)\;=\;e^{-i\Theta_a(t)}\,a_2^\dagger a_1,\qquad W(t)\,f_2^\dagger f_1\,W^\dagger(t)\;=\;e^{-i\Theta_f(t)}\,f_2^\dagger f_1,
$$
with
$$
\begin{align*}
\Theta_a(t)&=\;\tfrac{U}{\hbar}(n_1^f-n_2^f)\,t \;+\; \chi\sin(\omega t+\phi),\\
\Theta_f(t)&=\;\tfrac{1}{\hbar}\bigl[\Delta_f+U(n_1^a-n_2^a)\bigr]\,t \;+\; \chi\sin(\omega t+\phi),
\end{align*}
$$
each the dynamical phase $\hbar^{-1}\!\int^t\!\Delta E_\alpha(t')dt'$ between the two Fock configurations connected by the hop. Therefore
$$
\widetilde H(t)\;=\;-J\Bigl[\,e^{-i\Theta_a(t)}\,a_2^\dagger a_1 \;+\; e^{-i\Theta_f(t)}\,f_2^\dagger f_1 \;+\; \mathrm{H.c.}\,\Bigr].
$$

**Step 4 — Jacobi–Anger expansion.** Substituting $e^{-i\chi\sin(\omega t+\phi)}=\sum_m\mathcal J_m(\chi)e^{-im(\omega t+\phi)}$ keeps the full harmonic structure,
$$
\begin{align*}
e^{-i\Theta_a(t)}&=\;\sum_m \mathcal J_m(\chi)\,e^{-im\phi}\,\exp\!\left[-i\!\left(\tfrac{U}{\hbar}(n_1^f-n_2^f)+m\omega\right)t\right],\\
e^{-i\Theta_f(t)}&=\;\sum_m \mathcal J_m(\chi)\,e^{-im\phi}\,\exp\!\left[-i\!\left(\tfrac{\Delta_f+U(n_1^a-n_2^a)}{\hbar}+m\omega\right)t\right].
\end{align*}
$$
Each hopping channel carries a Bessel weight $\mathcal J_m(\chi)\,e^{-im\phi}$.

**Step 5 — Resonance selection.** In the leading rotating-wave approximation only harmonics satisfying $\Delta E_\alpha/\hbar+m\omega\simeq 0$ survive — off-resonant terms are suppressed by $J/(\hbar\omega)\ll 1$.

- **$a$-hopping** ($N_f=1$, $\hbar\omega\simeq U$). The energy mismatch is $\pm U$ on the two $f$-position sectors $P^f_\pm$, so the resonance condition picks the one-photon channels $\nu=\pm 1$. Collecting the Bessel weights $\mathcal J_{\pm 1}(\chi)\,e^{\pm i\phi}$ on $P^f_\pm$ yields $H_a^{(0)}$ of the lemma.
- **$f$-hopping** ($N_a=1$, $\Delta_f=U$). The energy mismatch is $0$ on one $a$-position sector and $2U$ on the other, so the resonance condition picks the zero- and two-photon channels $\nu=0,\,2$. Collecting the Bessel weights $\mathcal J_0(\chi)$ on $P^a_0$ and $\mathcal J_2(\chi)\,e^{2i\phi}$ on $P^a_2$ (using $\mathcal J_{-2}(\chi)=\mathcal J_2(\chi)$ for the H.c. partner) yields $H_f^{(0)}$ of the lemma.

$\square$

:::




# Dipole resonant Rydberg encoding

Another choice of encoding use two Rydberg states and their dipole resonant transition to encode the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge field.
In the Rydberg-array proposal of @domanti2024floquet, Floquet engineering of a periodically driven $XY$-chain reproduces the same 1-D $\mathbb Z_2$ gauge-field Hamiltonian. Odd-site qubits encode matter and even-site qubits encode the gauge link; the physical Hamiltonian is

$$
\begin{align*}
H_{XY}(t) &= \sum_{i=1}^{N_a-1} J\bigl(\sigma^+_i \sigma^-_{i+1} + \mathrm{H.c.}\bigr) + \sum_i h^{(l)}_i(t)\,\sigma^z_i + \sum_i h^{(t)}_i(t)\,\sigma^x_i,\\
h^{(l)}_i(t) &= \tfrac{1}{2}\bigl[(-1)^i\delta h + \eta\,\omega_d\cos(\omega_d t + \phi_i)\bigr]\,\delta_{i,\mathrm{odd}},\\
h^{(t)}_i &= \tfrac{\Omega}{2}\,\delta_{i,\mathrm{even}}.
\end{align*}
$$

The three-body assisted hopping $\sigma^+_i\sigma^z_j\sigma^-_k$ is *not* produced by a naive rotating-wave approximation: it arises from a **second-order** high-frequency expansion after a first-order Bessel-zero cancellation of the bare $XY$ exchange.

:::{#lem-XYexpansion .callout-important icon="false"}
## (Rotating-frame Hamiltonian expansion)
The expansion of the dynamic Hamiltonian $H_{XY}(t)$ is given by:
$$
\begin{align*}
H_{\mathrm{eff}} = \sum_{i\,\mathrm{even}} \frac{\Omega}{2} \sigma^x_i + \sum_{i\,\mathrm{odd}} (-1)^i \frac{\delta h}{2} \sigma^z_i + \sum_{\langle i, j, k \rangle} \frac{J^2}{\hbar\omega_d} \chi_{ik} \sigma^+_i \sigma^z_j \sigma^-_k + O(\omega_d^{-2}),
\end{align*}
$$
where $\chi_{jk} = \sum_{m>0}\frac{2i}{m}\,[\mathcal J_m(\eta)]^{2}\,\sin\!\bigl[m(\phi_k-\phi_j)\bigr]$.
:::

:::{.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Proof sketch
Define the odd-site phase
$$
\theta_i(t)\;\equiv\;\eta\,\delta_{i,\mathrm{odd}}\,\sin(\omega_d t+\phi_i),
$$
and the unitary
$$
U_d(t)\;=\;\exp\!\left[\,i\sum_i \frac{\theta_i(t)}{2}\,\sigma^z_i\right].
$$
Under $\ket\psi\mapsto U_d(t)\ket\psi$ the rotated Hamiltonian is $\widetilde H(t) = U_d(t)\,H_{XY}(t)\,U_d^\dagger(t)\,+\,i\hbar\dot U_d(t)\,U_d^\dagger(t)$; the second term exactly cancels the periodic longitudinal drive on odd sites. The static $\sigma^z$ field on odd sites and the static $\sigma^x$ field on even sites pass through, while ladder operators acquire $U_d\,\sigma^\pm_i\,U_d^\dagger = e^{\pm i\theta_i(t)}\sigma^\pm_i$. Each hopping link therefore picks up a relative phase
$$
\sigma^+_i\sigma^-_{i+1}\;\longmapsto\;e^{i[\theta_i(t)-\theta_{i+1}(t)]}\,\sigma^+_i\sigma^-_{i+1}.
$$
Because every link joins exactly one odd and one even site,
$$
\begin{align*}
\theta_i(t)-\theta_{i+1}(t)&=s_i\,\eta\sin(\omega_d t+\varphi_i) = \eta\sin(\omega_d t+\varphi_i + s_i\pi)\\
s_i\;&=\;\begin{cases}+1,& i\,\mathrm{odd}\\ -1,& i\,\mathrm{even}\end{cases},\qquad
\varphi_i\;=\;\begin{cases}\phi_i,& i\,\mathrm{odd}\\ \phi_{i+1},& i\,\mathrm{even}\end{cases}.
\end{align*}
$$

Substituting $e^{i\eta\sin\theta}=\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}\mathcal J_m(\eta)\,e^{im\theta}$ decomposes the rotating-frame hopping into Fourier harmonics, giving $\widetilde H(t) = H_0 + \sum_{m\neq 0}V_m\,e^{im\omega_d t}$, with
$$
\begin{align*}
H_0 &= H_{\mathrm{stat}}\;+\;V_0,\\
H_{\mathrm{stat}} &= \sum_{i\,\mathrm{odd}}\frac{(-1)^i\delta h}{2}\sigma^z_i\;+\;\sum_{i\,\mathrm{even}}\frac{\Omega}{2}\sigma^x_i,\\
V_0 &= J\mathcal J_0(\eta)\sum_i\bigl(\sigma^+_i\sigma^-_{i+1}+\mathrm{H.c.}\bigr),\\
V_m &= J\sum_i\Bigl[\mathcal J_m(s_i\eta)\,e^{im\varphi_i}\,\sigma^+_i\sigma^-_{i+1}\;+\;\mathcal J_m(-s_i\eta)\,e^{im\varphi_i}\,\sigma^-_i\sigma^+_{i+1}\Bigr],
\end{align*}
$$
where $\mathcal J_0(-\eta)=\mathcal J_0(\eta)$ collapses the two link orientations in $V_0$.
Setting the drive amplitude at the first zero of $\mathcal J_0$,
$$
\eta\;=\;\nu_1\;\simeq\;2.405,\qquad \mathcal J_0(\nu_1)\;=\;0,
$$
gives $V_0=0$, so the zeroth-order Hamiltonian collapses to $H_0=H_{\mathrm{stat}}$ and the gauge-breaking direct $XY$ exchange is coherently suppressed [@schweizer2019floquet; @domanti2024floquet].


Use van Vleck expansion (see [Lemma van Vleck expansion](theory/Posts/Floquet/Floquet.qmd#lem-exp_ham)) to expand this rotating-frame Hamiltonian.
The leading non-trivial correction is $\sum_{m>0}[V_m,V_{-m}]/(m\hbar\omega_d)$.

For an odd–even–odd triplet $\langle i,j,k\rangle$ (so $i,k$ odd and $j=i+1$ even, $k=j+1$), the matter-conserving two-body building blocks are $A_{ij}=\sigma^+_i\sigma^-_j$ and $B_{jk}=\sigma^+_j\sigma^-_k$, whose Fourier coefficients in $V_m$ read
$$
A_{ij}\bigm|_{V_m}\;=\;J\mathcal J_m(\eta)\,e^{im\phi_i},\qquad B_{jk}\bigm|_{V_m}\;=\;J\mathcal J_m(-\eta)\,e^{im\phi_k}\;=\;J(-1)^m\mathcal J_m(\eta)\,e^{im\phi_k},
$$
using $\mathcal J_m(-\eta)=(-1)^m\mathcal J_m(\eta)$. The on-site $SU(2)$ identity
$$
[\sigma^+_i\sigma^-_j,\,\sigma^+_j\sigma^-_k]\;=\;-\,\sigma^+_i\sigma^z_j\sigma^-_k
$$
turns two two-body virtual exchanges into a three-body assisted hopping. The two cross-pairings in $[V_m,V_{-m}]$ produce the destructive sum
$$
J^{2}\mathcal J_m^{2}(\eta)\,\bigl[-\,e^{im(\phi_i-\phi_k)}\;+\;e^{im(\phi_k-\phi_i)}\bigr]\,\sigma^+_i\sigma^z_j\sigma^-_k
\;=\;2i\,J^{2}\mathcal J_m^{2}(\eta)\,\sin\!\bigl[m(\phi_k-\phi_i)\bigr]\,\sigma^+_i\sigma^z_j\sigma^-_k,
$$
and collecting all $m>0$,
$$
\begin{align*}
H_{\mathrm{eff}} &= H_{\mathrm{stat}}\;+\;\sum_{\langle i,j,k\rangle}\frac{J^{2}}{\hbar\omega_d}\,\chi_{ik}\,\sigma^+_i\sigma^z_j\sigma^-_k\;+\;\mathrm{H.c.}\;+\;O(\omega_d^{-2}),\\
\chi_{ik} &= \sum_{m>0}\frac{2i}{m}\,[\mathcal J_m(\eta)]^{2}\,\sin\!\bigl[m(\phi_k-\phi_i)\bigr].
\end{align*}
$$
$\chi_{ik}$ is purely imaginary, so $J^{2}\chi_{ik}/(\hbar\omega_d)$ is imaginary and the $+\mathrm{H.c.}$ restores Hermiticity.

**Step 5 — Phase-selective gauge invariance and identification.** Because $\chi_{ik}\propto\sin[m(\phi_k-\phi_i)]$, every triplet whose end-points see identical driving phases ($\phi_k=\phi_i\bmod 2\pi$) is annihilated by destructive interference. The selection rules are:

- **odd–even–odd:** the two odd end-points carry independent phases $\phi_i\neq\phi_k$, so $\chi_{ik}\neq 0$ — *kept*.
- **even–odd–even:** the two even end-points have no longitudinal drive, equivalent to identical phases, so $\chi_{ik}=0$ — *cancelled*.
- **other long-range assisted hoppings:** suppressed by an appropriate choice of $\{\phi_i\}$.

Only the gauge-invariant assisted hopping $\sigma^+_{2n-1}\sigma^z_{2n}\sigma^-_{2n+1}$ survives. Identifying
$$
a_n^\dagger\;=\;\sigma^+_{2n-1},\qquad \tau^z_{n-\frac12}\;=\;\sigma^z_{2n-2},\qquad \tau^x_{n-\frac12}\;=\;\sigma^x_{2n-2},
$$
recovers the $\mathbb Z_2$ lattice gauge Hamiltonian $H_{\mathbb Z_2}$ stated at the top of this note, with effective couplings
$$
J_t\;=\;\frac{J^{2}}{\hbar\omega_d}\,\chi,\qquad h\;=\;\frac{\Omega}{2},\qquad \mu\;=\;\delta h,
$$
where $\chi$ is the value of $\chi_{ik}$ on the selected triplet.

**Note (sign of the staggered mass).** On odd sites $i=2n-1$ the literal $(-1)^i\equiv -1$ is constant, so the bare $(-1)^i\delta h\,\sigma^z_i/2$ in $h^{(l)}_i(t)$ is a *uniform* longitudinal shift on the matter sites rather than a staggered mass. To recover the staggered matter mass $\mu(-1)^n a_n^\dagger a_n$ one replaces $(-1)^i\to(-1)^{(i-1)/2}$ on odd $i$ — equivalently $(-1)^n$ in matter index $n=(i-1)/2$ — at the level of $h^{(l)}_i$; this is the convention used in @domanti2024floquet.

:::
